number.why: The served HR 0.92 (95% CI 0.80–1.06) matches the primary MACE endpoint, omega-3 versus placebo, in the intention-to-treat analysis over the full randomized intervention period. It is supported as an HR, not as the packet's nominal RR estimand.

quotes.span: During a median follow-up of 5.3 years, a major cardiovascular event occurred in 386 participants in the n-3 group and in 419 in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.92; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.80 to 1.06; P=0.24).
Primary endpoints were major cardiovascular events (composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, and cardiovascular mortality) and total invasive cancer.

Treatment-effect analyses were based on the intention-to-treat principle, as described in the companion paper on vitamin D. Primary analyses were based on Cox proportional hazards models controlling for age, sex, and randomization to vitamin D.
Study medication ceased as planned on December 31, 2017, yielding a median intervention period of 5.3 years (range 3.8-6.1 years).

entry.why: The intervention and blinded randomized placebo-controlled design qualify. Population fit is partial if 'at cardiovascular risk' requires risk enrichment: recruitment was age-based in a usual-risk primary-prevention population, although participants with cardiovascular risk factors were included. The question does not explicitly define an elevated-risk threshold, so this is a scope qualification rather than definite exclusion.

quotes.span: Large trials of n-3 supplements for primary prevention of cardiovascular disease in a general population selected only on age and not on vascular risk factors such as diabetes or dyslipidemia are lacking.

This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2×2 factorial trial tested the benefits and risks of vitamin D 3 (2000 IU/day) and n-3 fatty acids (1 g/day fish-oil capsule containing 840 mg of n-3 fatty acids including eicosapentaenoic acid [EPA, 460 mg] + docosahexaenoic acid [DHA, 380 mg]) in the primary prevention of cardiovascular disease and cancer among 25,871 men aged ≥50 and women aged ≥55, including 5,106 African Americans.
our trial, which tested n-3 fatty acids for primary prevention in a usual-risk population

missed: No additional finding changes either verdict. Two metadata corrections are warranted: the recorded dose '3 g' contradicts the quoted 1 g/day fish-oil capsule, and adjustment is established by the quoted Cox-model methods rather than UNRESOLVED. HR confirmation also does not resolve whether an RR-targeted synthesis permits HRs.
